transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because... well, I just can't shake this certainty that I'm being punished. It's about my father, and how I let him decline. My sister tries to tell me otherwise, she even shows me the doctor's notes and says I've done everything right, but... it doesn't matter. It still feels like some kind of judgment has already been passed on me, and I'm just living through the consequences.
Do you often feel guilty or that you are a bad person, even when others tell you that you've done nothing wrong?

Yes, constantly. I just... I keep going over every single decision I made about my father's appointments. And every tense conversation I've had with my relatives about it. I replay it all, and I always end up feeling like I'm just a selfish daughter. It even spills over into my job... I feel like a completely useless employee, too. I really just feel like I deserve whatever happens to me, no matter what my sister or anyone else says.
Do these feelings of guilt and worthlessness happen even when you're not thinking about your father or your job?

I'm not really sure, honestly. It feels like I'm almost always thinking about my father or how I'm failing at work, so it's hard to separate it all. The guilt is just... it's just always there, hovering over me. I don't know if I've really noticed a time when it isn't tied to one of those things, because they're always on my mind.
Can you recall any period in the last few weeks when you weren't thinking about your father or work, and if so, did the guilt or feeling of worthlessness still follow you during that time?

I really can't. It's... it's just a constant loop in my head. If I'm not agonizing over my dad and what I should have done differently, I'm stressing about how I'm messing everything up at work. I don't think there's been a single moment in the last few weeks where my mind was just quiet. So, I don't know if the guilt would still be there without those thoughts, because those thoughts just never stop.

Even though your mind is often on your father or work, can you imagine a situation where those thoughts stopped—say, during sleep or a distraction—would the guilt or sense of worthlessness still return afterward, even for a moment?

I mean... yeah, I suppose so. Even if I try to distract myself, or right when I wake up before my brain fully kicks in, it's like the feeling is already waiting for me. I just... I keep going over every decision I made about my father's appointments, and every tense conversation I've had with my relatives. It always comes back to that. I just end up feeling like I'm a selfish daughter, and a completely useless employee. It's just this heavy feeling that I deserve whatever happens to me.
Even if you were to imagine a situation where all your current stressors—like your father’s condition and work—were suddenly gone, do you think you would still feel the same guilt and worthlessness?

I honestly don't know how to even picture that. Like I was just saying, my mind is completely stuck replaying all those decisions about his appointments and the tense conversations with my relatives. It's hard to separate the actual situation from the feeling. 

But... even if the stressors magically went away today, I think I'd still feel this way. That feeling of being a selfish daughter and a useless employee... it just feels permanent now. I really do feel like I deserve whatever happens to me, whether the stress is there or not.
Even if you weren't thinking about your father or work, do you think you would still feel the same sense of guilt and worthlessness?

I know I just said this, but it's hard to even imagine not thinking about it. I just keep going over every single decision I made about my dad's appointments, and every tense conversation I've had with my relatives. It all just circles back to me feeling like I'm a selfish daughter and a useless employee. I really do feel like I just deserve whatever happens to me, even if I wasn't actively thinking about those specific things. The feeling is just always there.
Have you ever experienced a time when you didn't feel this guilt or worthlessness, even for a short while, like during a vacation or when something positive happened in your life?

Not recently, no. Even if I try to take a break or something positive happens... I feel like a broken record here, but my brain just won't let it go. I just keep going over every decision I made about my father's appointments. And those tense conversations I had with my relatives... they just constantly replay in my head. 

It kind of ruins any good moment, because I always end up right back to feeling like I'm a selfish daughter and a completely useless employee. Like I've been saying, I just feel like I deserve whatever happens to me. So, no, it doesn't really lift.
Even if you weren't thinking about your father’s condition or your job performance at all, do you think you would still feel that same sense of guilt and worthlessness?

I know you've asked me this a few different ways now, but... it's just hard to separate it all. Like I said before, my mind is just stuck. I keep going over every single decision I made about my father's appointments, and every tense conversation with my relatives. It just plays on a loop. 

Even if I try to imagine not thinking about those things, it always comes back to the same place. I just end up feeling like I'm a selfish daughter and a useless employee. It's this heavy feeling that I just deserve whatever bad things happen to me. So, yes, I think the feeling would still be there, because it's just who I am now.
